notes:
Six bullets, six real actions -- an unusually clean page. Two of them are ??? examines at the same grid, and the second one (bullet 5) is the interesting judgement: it produces nothing but a line of text, so a keyword reader would drop it as flavour, but the page says outright that Rukususu will not accept the Ominous Skull until you have read it. It is a step. Neither ??? can carry a marker (??? is in OBJECT_DENY) but both keep their rung.

The two fights have no stated location. Sensenmann and Xibalba are named, the zone is not; 'Abyssea - Grauberg' is carried down from the quest's own zone rather than invented, and both steps are demoted to medium for it. Bullet 4 also never says HOW the molar spawns Xibalba -- no ??? , no NPC -- so the target stays none rather than guessing at a pop point.

'Skyrend' in bullet 2 is an area inside Abyssea - Grauberg, not a zone; it does not resolve and is kept as a note. Fame 'agra' is an Abyssea zone code, not one of the nine regions, so it gates nothing and only the raw is kept. The Decaying Molar can be bought on the Auction House instead of farmed, which the evidence covers either way since holding it is what is observed.

notes:
Seven bullets, three steps. Bullets 3 through 7 are the battlefield's rules and the fight's tactics -- time limit, party size, no Trusts, job pairings, sleep resistance, skillchains, and finally 'you will receive your reward', which is an outcome. Only bullets 1 and 2 are things you do, plus the fight itself, which I have kept as one step because the page treats the three enemies as a single encounter ('once all three are defeated').

The wiki's menu option in bullet 2 came through the prepass as an empty string -- 'select "" at the Dark Miasma' -- so the exact selection cannot be recorded; the Dark Miasma itself is the entity and is named.

'Quest Reqs' holds two different things: Promathia Mission 7-5, which is a real prerequisite and goes in prev even though the Previous field is blank, and 'Letter from Shikaree X', which is not a prerequisite at all -- it is the key item bullet 1 hands you, and so it is step 1's evidence. The page does not say the letter must be held to enter the battlefield, so it is not listed among step 2's items.

all three. 30 minutes, up to 6 party members, no Trusts. Shikaree X is BST/NIN and re-summons the Rabbit if it dies first, so kill her before it; the Rabbit resists sleep but not bind or gravity. Shikaree Y is DRK/MNK. Both sisters shrug off sleep, build TP fast and skillchain with each other. Bullets 3 to 7 are rules, tactics and the reward -- none is a separate action. notes:
This is a LOOP fifteen times over, not a fifteen-rung ladder: talk to Maat on a job, fight him at the BC area he names, come back, change job, repeat. Three steps is the honest shape. Fifteen fight steps would be wrong twice over -- the ladder would claim an order the game does not impose, and nothing in the packets reports which jobs are already done, so it could never advance past the first.

The fifteen job names in bullet 2's sub-bullets are NOT a job gate. 'jobs' means 'only these jobs may take this quest'; here every job may, and the requirement is that you eventually beat him on all of them. Putting them in jobs would lock the quest to fifteen jobs at once and gate it wrongly forever, so jobs stays empty and the list lives in the step note.

Bullet 3's 'the level required to fight Maat is at least level 66' contradicts the header's 'Level: None'. The header is kept -- the 66 belongs to the Shattering Stars fights this quest is built on, and level is a prereq predicate, not advice. Bullet 4 is a diagnostic aid, not a step: talking to Teyrnon in Feretory only tells you which jobs you have already cleared, by which Instinct prices are halved. Nobody has to do it.

steps.note: once per job. He asks for that job's Testimony and names the BC area to meet him at. The Testimonies are per-job and the page names none of them, so none is recorded.

notes:
A short Mog Garden chain, entirely in one zone, with no items and no key items anywhere in the walkthrough -- so no step carries evidence and the ladder relies on the session latch throughout. That is the correct answer here, not a reach.

The baby sheep is the one thing that cannot be marked. The page calls it 'your baby sheep' and 'a baby sheep'; the description calls it 'the bodyguard's lamb'; the next quest, Feeding Frenzy, does no better ('your baby sheep', 'the sheep'). None of those is an entity name, so the target is none/null rather than a guess at Lamb or Sheep. The step keeps its rung.

Steps 2 and 4 are both Chacharoon but they are genuinely separated by the sheep, so they are not collapsed. The five key items under Item Reqs -- 'Fields And Fertilizing' and the rest -- are the Mog Garden rank-up books that make up the 'Level 4 Mog Garden' requirement, i.e. gates, not things this quest has you fetch; neither they nor 'Recruit Susuroon at least once' has a slot in the schema, so both are recorded here only.

notes:
The trap on this page is that it names three people you never go to. Bullet 1 says to deliver the receipt to Prince Pieuje or Prince Trion in Chateau d'Oraguille, and both are real, resolvable NPCs -- but you never reach either of them. Guilerme takes the receipt at the bridge, asks which prince, and walks it in himself. A verb-scanner would put a step in Chateau d'Oraguille; there is none, and the quest never leaves the two San d'Oria city zones. The prince is a dialogue choice, and getting it wrong costs 100 gil, not the quest.

Bullet 2 is nothing but walking directions -- out of the shop, west into Victory Square, north through Victory Arch, north again -- so it is folded into step 2's note rather than made a travel step. The page never gives Guilerme a grid, only 'near the bridge into the Chateau', so grid stays null; the zone is Northern San d'Oria because that is where bullet 2 leaves you.

notes:
The best ladder in this batch: seven steps, three of them carrying evidence, across three zones. The page writes 'Thyme moss', 'Cough medicine' and 'Scroll of treasure' in plain prose with no [KI] tag, which invites recording them as inventory items -- none of the three is an item. All three are key items (153, 154, 155) and none exists in res/items.lua at all, so getting the kind wrong would have silently cost this quest every evidence point it has.

Bullet 3's sub-bullet is where you actually get the moss, in Davoi, and it is a step of its own -- the parent bullet is only Amaura asking for it. Bullets 6 and 7 are the reverse: 6 says where the scroll points and 7 is the click, so they merge into one step.

The quest ends on an object, not a person. The 3,000 gil comes out of the signpost in East Ronfaure, so there is no hand-in and none is invented. Bullet 1's note that the quest does not enter your log until the item hunt begins is real but unobservable, and the optional extra questions to Nenne are not a step.

notes:
Four bullets, five steps, all in one zone. The extra step is Kupipi (A), who is a sub-bullet precondition -- 'you'll need to speak to her beforehand if you've never done so' -- so she is marked optional rather than made a ladder position. She stands in the same grid square as Apururu (A), so nothing is lost either way.

The Bottomless Box is the target of step 4, not Kopuro-Popuro (A): he only tells you to go and charm it. That is the sentence-fragment trap -- he is the NPC the bullet names, the box is the thing you interact with. Emoting at an object is not an examine, so the kind is other.

The one real loss here is the evidence. 'Ripe starfruit' appears TWICE in res/key_items.lua, and the resolver rejects non-unique key-item names outright rather than guessing an id, so this evidence will be dropped at validation and step 4 will keep its place and its marker but not its observability. It is recorded anyway because the name is the page's and correct; the fault is in the resource table, and a human should see it rather than have it quietly turn into null. Fame 'atah' is an Abyssea zone code, not one of the nine regions, so it gates nothing.
